paper_metadata.title: Quantum Stochastic Walks for Portfolio Optimization: Theory and Implementation on Financial Networks

experiments.description: Scenario-based quantum stochastic walk portfolio optimization on the Top-100 S&P constituents, evaluated under six hand-designed parameter presets and five quantum-classical mixing values on 1-year and 2-year rolling training windows with quarterly rebalancing.

algorithm.variant: Quantum stochastic walk (QSW) / quantum PageRank-based portfolio optimizer with dual-channel coherent + stochastic dynamics
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate density operator until ||rho(t+1) - rho(t)||_1 <= 1e-8 or t >= 5000
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialize rho(0) = I/n (uniform superposition / maximally mixed state)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Assets are nodes in a weighted directed graph; off-diagonal weights use exp(alpha * SR_j - beta * Sigma_ij), diagonal self-loops use exp(lambda * SR_i). The stochastic channel uses a row-normalized weight matrix and Google matrix; the coherent channel uses a Hamiltonian with diagonal terms proportional to Sharpe ratio and off-diagonal terms proportional to normalized covariance.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Portfolio weights are obtained from the stationary distribution of the QSW density matrix; the construction is designed to favor high-Sharpe assets and penalize correlated assets while maintaining diversification.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Long-only, fully invested portfolio with weights normalized to sum to 1; diversification emerges from the stochastic channel rather than explicit cardinality constraints.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_ii = -gamma1 * SR_i; H_ij = gamma2 * Sigma_hat_ij for i != j, where Sigma_hat_ij = (Sigma_ij - Sigma_min) / (Sigma_max - Sigma_min)

problem_instance.description: Top 100 U.S. equities by market capitalization, including large-cap technology, financial, healthcare, and other sector names.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance historical prices for Top-100 S&P constituents

dataset_specification.description: Daily adjusted close prices from 2016-01-01 to 2024-12-31; training windows of 1 year (252 trading days) and 2 years (504 trading days); backtesting from 2018-01-02 to 2024-12-31; quarterly rebalancing; log returns and sample covariance computed from the training window.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute daily log returns, sample covariance matrix, mean returns, volatilities, Sharpe ratios, weight matrix W, Hamiltonian H, and Google matrix G from the training window.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Extract portfolio weights from the stationary density matrix diagonal and normalize to sum to 1; evaluate Sharpe, volatility, turnover, HHI, effective number of stocks, and cumulative return in backtests.

speedup_claims.conditions: Scenario analysis on Top-100 S&P constituents with 1-year and 2-year training windows
speedup_claims.caveats: No algorithmic runtime speedup is claimed; the paper reports performance and trading-efficiency improvements instead.

experiments.description: Comprehensive 625-point grid search for QSW portfolio optimization on the Top-100 S&P universe, exploring the full four-dimensional hyperparameter space across 1-year and 2-year rolling windows.

algorithm.variant: Quantum stochastic walk (QSW) / quantum PageRank-based portfolio optimizer with full hyperparameter grid search
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate density operator until ||rho(t+1) - rho(t)||_1 <= 1e-8 or t >= 5000
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialize rho(0) = I/n; grid search over all parameter combinations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same graph encoding as the scenario study: nodes are assets, directed edge weights are exp(alpha * SR_j - beta * Sigma_ij), self-loops are exp(lambda * SR_i), and the coherent Hamiltonian uses normalized covariance and Sharpe ratios.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Stationary distribution of the QSW defines portfolio weights; the grid search seeks parameter settings that maximize Sharpe and Sharpe/turnover efficiency while maintaining low concentration.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Long-only, fully invested; diversification and turnover control are induced by the QSW dynamics and parameter choices rather than explicit hard constraints.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_ii = -gamma1 * SR_i; H_ij = gamma2 * Sigma_hat_ij for i != j

problem_instance.description: Top 100 U.S. equities by market capitalization, evaluated over rolling 1-year and 2-year look-back windows.
problem_instance.dataset_name: Yahoo Finance historical prices for Top-100 S&P constituents

dataset_specification.description: Daily adjusted close prices from 2016-01-01 to 2024-12-31; 625 parameter combinations; 28 non-overlapping evaluation periods per look-back setting; monthly rebalancing in the grid-search description; outputs include Sharpe, volatility, turnover, efficiency, HHI, and effective-stock count.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute returns, covariance, Sharpe ratios, weight matrix, Hamiltonian, and Google matrix for each grid point and rolling window.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Record metrics to CSV; compare against MPT benchmark and summarize distributions, correlations, heatmaps, and top-10 configurations.

speedup_claims.conditions: 625-point grid search on Top-100 universe; GPU-accelerated cuPyNumeric implementation
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports computational throughput (3 hours for the full grid on an NVIDIA A100) but does not compare against a CPU baseline or provide an explicit speedup factor.

experiments.description: Robustness validation of the QSW portfolio optimizer across 50 random 100-stock subsets of the S&P 500, each re-running the full 625-point grid on a 2-year look-back window.

algorithm.variant: Quantum stochastic walk (QSW) / quantum PageRank-based portfolio optimizer with multi-universe robustness testing
algorithm.convergence_criteria: Iterate density operator until ||rho(t+1) - rho(t)||_1 <= 1e-8 or t >= 5000
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initialize rho(0) = I/n; full grid search repeated independently for each random universe

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Same asset-graph encoding as the other QSW experiments; each random universe rebuilds the factor matrix and graph weights from the selected 100 stocks.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Use the stationary distribution of the QSW to generate portfolio weights and evaluate whether the best configuration generalizes across random universes.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Long-only, fully invested; diversification and turnover are controlled by the QSW parameters.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H_ii = -gamma1 * SR_i; H_ij = gamma2 * Sigma_hat_ij for i != j

problem_instance.description: Fifty independent random draws of 100 stocks from the S&P 500 universe, with the full QSW grid re-optimized on each draw.

dataset_specification.description: Each replication samples 100 names uniformly at random from the S&P 500; daily adjusted close prices from Yahoo Finance; 2-year look-back; backtesting from 2018-01-02 to 2024-12-31; quarterly rebalancing; 31,350 back-tests total across 50 draws.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: For each random universe, rebuild the covariance matrix, Sharpe ratios, weight matrix, Hamiltonian, and Google matrix from the sampled stocks.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Compare best-per-draw QSW portfolio against the corresponding MPT optimum and a 5%-turnover S&P 500 proxy; aggregate win rates and distributional statistics across 50 draws.

speedup_claims.conditions: 50 random 100-stock universes; 2-year look-back; full 625-point grid repeated per universe
speedup_claims.caveats: No computational speedup is claimed; the paper reports robustness and performance win rates across universes.
